title: selectedDate never advances at local midnight while the Fuel tab stays open
steps: Fake the clock to 2026-09-30 23:55 local, load /fuel, then advance the clock (no reload/navigation) to 2026-10-01 00:10. Open Add Food and log a manual entry.
expected: Once local time crosses midnight, the page either re-derives selectedDate to the new day or clearly shows the entry is being logged to the prior day before saving.
actual: The Add Food dialog still read "Logging to ... Sep 30" after the clock crossed into Oct 1, and the saved row's date column was 2026-09-30 (stale) while eaten_at correctly captured the real 2026-10-01T06:10:00Z instant. The entry is silently misattributed to the wrong day in daily/weekly totals with zero on-screen indication.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-01.mjs console output (date=2026-09-30, eaten_at=2026-10-01T06:10:00+00:00, dialogHeader="Logging to Wed, Sep 30")
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:202 (selectedDate = useState(...) never re-derives from a live clock)

title: "Logging earlier" eaten_at across the DST fall-back transition
steps: On 2026-11-01 (America/Denver DST fall-back date), toggle "Logging earlier", force meal type to Dinner (default 19:00 local), fill calories, submit.
expected: eaten_at reflects 19:00 local time using the correct post-fallback MST offset (UTC-7), i.e. 2026-11-02T02:00:00Z.
actual: ok — eaten_at=2026-11-02T02:00:00.000Z, exactly matching the expected UTC instant. No DST bug found.

title: Per-row protein/carbs/fats render as blank (not "0") when the underlying fields are null
steps: Directly insert a food_entries row with calories=320 and protein_grams/carbs_grams/fats_grams all null. Load /fuel.
expected: Calories render correctly and macro fields render as a sane number (e.g. 0), not empty/NaN.
actual: Calories render fine (320, no NaN) and the day's aggregate ring/goal bars are null-safe. But the per-row protein/carbs/fats cells are left completely BLANK instead of "0" in both the desktop macro grid (3/3 empty spans) and the mobile inline strip ("P · C · F" with no digits before each letter).
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-03.mjs console output + row innerHTML snippet
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:~2171-2196 (entry.protein_grams / entry.carbs_grams / entry.fats_grams read with no || 0 fallback)

title: Serving amount 0.00001 passes validation and logs a near-zero ghost entry
steps: USDA-search "chicken breast", select a result, set Amount to 0.00001, tap Add Food.
expected: An implausible near-zero serving amount is rejected or floored before saving, not silently accepted as a real entry.
actual: Accepted. submitDisabled stayed false. Row created: calories=0, serving_size=0.00001, serving_unit=g — a phantom entry with no nutritional signal that still inflates the day's item count.
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:3145 (disabled check is (parseFloat(newFood.serving_amount)||0) <= 0, which lets 0.00001 through since it's > 0)

title: Serving amount has no upper bound — 10000 g of almonds accepted as-is
steps: USDA-search "almonds", select a 100g-basis result (unit already defaults to grams), type 10000 into the Amount field, tap Add Food.
expected: A 10 kg single serving (~57,900 kcal) is flagged or blocked as implausible before saving, or at minimum the app asks for confirmation.
actual: Accepted with no warning: row saved with calories=57900, serving_size=10000. No page error and no visible ring/arc corruption (problems=0), so the day's UI didn't break, but nothing stops an obviously implausible single entry from being logged silently.
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx (Amount input, ~line 2807, has min="0" step="0.5" but no max)

title: Delete entry has no confirm and no undo (double-tap itself is safe)
steps: Log a tagged entry, then fire two near-simultaneous clicks (no await between them) on its Trash icon before the first request's response returns.
expected: Per judge rule ("mistakes can be undone"), a destructive delete should have either a confirm step or an undo path. Double-tap itself should not duplicate errors or corrupt state.
actual: Data integrity was fine under double-tap: exactly one row removed (rowsAfter=0), zero click errors, zero page problems — deleteFoodMutation's lack of an isPending guard did not cause a visible double-delete failure in practice. However, confirmed there is genuinely zero recovery path: no confirm dialog before deleting, and no "Undo" action appears in the "Entry deleted" toast (hasUndo=false). A single mis-tap permanently loses a logged entry with no way back.
suspectFile: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:1120-1128 (deleteFoodMutation, no onError handler, no undo), :2222 (trash button, no confirm, no disabled={deleteFoodMutation.isPending} guard)

title: Double-tap "mark as eaten" on a planned item
steps: Seed a tagged planned:true row for today, then fire two near-simultaneous clicks on its "mark as eaten" checkbox before the first mutation's response returns.
expected: The entry flips planned:false exactly once, with no duplicate row and no data corruption.
actual: ok — exactly 1 row remained, planned correctly flipped true -> false, zero click errors, zero page problems. togglePlannedMutation's missing isPending guard did not cause a duplicate-toggle bug in practice (a second concurrent update to the same field is a no-op).

title: Edit an entry's amount, reload before the update lands
steps: Log a tagged entry (calories=200, serving_size=1), open Edit, change the serving amount to 3, tap Save Changes, then immediately reload() (network delayed 4s via route interception so the reload reliably wins the race).
expected: Either the edit is lost cleanly (old value survives intact) or it completes and is reflected after reload — never a row left with a mix of old and new fields (e.g. new serving_size but stale calories).
actual: ok on the specific edit-race question — the row survived unchanged (serving_size=1, calories=200, isOld=true), no partial/mixed state. updateFoodMutation's single combined .update() call is atomic at the DB layer as expected; no client-side optimistic write persisted a stale value either.

title: Reloading /fuel mid-navigation surfaces an uncaught pageerror from an unrelated program_workouts fetch
steps: Same setup as fuel-r1-08 (edit an entry, click Save, then page.reload() ~150ms later). Captured via drive.mjs's pageerror listener.
expected: Navigating away mid-fetch should not surface an uncaught JS error to the console; in-flight requests being aborted by navigation is a normal browser event and should be handled/swallowed (e.g. by react-query's abort handling), not thrown.
actual: report() captured a pageerror: ".../rest/v1/program_workouts?select=*&program_id=in.(...) due to access control checks." This fired once during the reload in the r1-08 run. It is not about food_entries and may be a global app-shell query (training program prefetch) rather than anything Fuel-specific; flagging since it's an uncaught error a real user could also hit by reloading/navigating away from /fuel while that background fetch is in flight. Caveat: only observed once, under an artificially delayed-network test harness — worth a verify pass to confirm it reproduces under normal (undelayed) network conditions too.
evidence: areas/fuel/scripts/r1-08.mjs report() output: problems=[{"type":"pageerror","msg":".../program_workouts?select=*&program_id=in.(...) due to access control checks."}]
suspectFile: unknown — likely a global training-plan query hook active on the app shell, not src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx itself
